paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: you've been raised with Christ, so you live from that, not toward it. Paul says you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God (Colossians 3:3). Then he says, "When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory" (Colossians 3:4). You don't have to earn a new identity. You already have one, and that's why Paul can tell you to set your mind on things above (Colossians 3:2).

So now the old stuff has to go, and Paul means ALL of it. Greed, anger, slander, lying: he says you took off the old self with its practices and put on the new self (Colossians 3:9-10). And the new self comes with a whole outfit: compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience, with love over all of it (Colossians 3:12, 14). I've worn a crusty apron before, and I promise you, once you've put on the clean one, you don't go digging the old one out of the laundry. Forgive as the Lord forgave you, and let Christ be all and in all, because that's what holds the whole body together (Colossians 3:11, 13).

And here's the best part: this isn't just for Sundays. Let the word of Christ richly dwell in you, let His peace rule your heart, and be thankful (Colossians 3:15-16). Then Paul says, "whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him" (Colossians 3:17). That covers your work, your words, your Tuesday afternoon, and yes, even your cookie number four hundred. So go put on the new, baker, and wear it everywhere.
